access_token.description: A bearer token to use as-is (it is not refreshed). Environment variable: `WSO2IS_ACCESS_TOKEN`.

base_url.description: Origin of the server, for example `https://localhost:9443` or `https://id.example.com`. Do not include a path. Environment variable: `WSO2IS_BASE_URL`.

ca_certificate.description: PEM encoded CA certificate(s) to trust in addition to the system roots. Environment variable: `WSO2IS_CA_CERTIFICATE` (PEM content or a file path).

client_id.description: Client ID of an OAuth2 application (usually an M2M application) authorized for the management APIs. Environment variable: `WSO2IS_CLIENT_ID`.

insecure_skip_verify.description: Skip TLS certificate verification. Use it only for test servers that use the default self-signed certificate. Environment variable: `WSO2IS_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY`.

max_retries.description: Retries for transient failures (HTTP 429/502/503/504 and connection errors). The default is `4`. Environment variable: `WSO2IS_MAX_RETRIES`.

organization_id.description: ID of a sub-organization (B2B) to manage instead of the root organization. Requests go to the organization-scoped (`/o/`) APIs. It needs the `client_id` and `client_secret` of an application that can use the `organization_switch` grant, or an `access_token` issued for the organization. Use a separate provider alias per organization; the ID may come from a `wso2is_organization` in the same configuration. Environment variable: `WSO2IS_ORGANIZATION_ID`.

password.description: Password for basic authentication. Environment variable: `WSO2IS_PASSWORD`.

request_timeout.description: Timeout of a single HTTP request in seconds. The default is `60`. Environment variable: `WSO2IS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`.

scopes.description: Scopes requested with the client credentials grant. The default is `["SYSTEM"]`, which WSO2 expands to every internal scope the application is authorized for. Environment variable: `WSO2IS_SCOPES` (space separated).

tenant_domain.description: Tenant (root organization) to manage. The default is `carbon.super`. Environment variable: `WSO2IS_TENANT_DOMAIN`.

username.description: Username for basic authentication (for example the super admin). Environment variable: `WSO2IS_USERNAME`.

block.description:
Manages [WSO2 Identity Server](https://wso2.com/identity-server/) 7.x through its management REST APIs.

Authenticate with one of: `username`/`password` (basic authentication), `client_id`/`client_secret` (OAuth2 client credentials of an application authorized for the management APIs), or a ready `access_token`. Credentials set in the provider block take precedence, as a group, over the `WSO2IS_*` environment variables.

active.description: Whether the action is active. The default is `true`. The server creates actions as inactive, so the provider activates them after it creates them.

allowed_headers.description: Request headers forwarded to the endpoint (token actions only).

allowed_parameters.description: Request parameters forwarded to the endpoint (token actions only).

attributes.description: The claim URIs that trigger the action when they change. The server sends these claims to the action. Only `pre_update_profile` actions use this setting.

authentication_properties.description: The credentials for the endpoint. Use `username` and `password` for `BASIC`, `accessToken` for `BEARER`, or `header` and `value` for `API_KEY`. The server never returns these values, so the provider cannot notice changes made outside Terraform.

authentication_type.description: How the server signs in to the endpoint. The allowed values are `NONE`, `BASIC`, `BEARER` and `API_KEY`.

endpoint_uri.description: HTTPS endpoint called by the server.

password_sharing_certificate.description: `pre_update_password` only: PEM certificate used to encrypt the shared password.

password_sharing_format.description: How the server shares the new password with the action, either `PLAIN_TEXT` or `SHA256_HASHED`. Only `pre_update_password` actions use this setting.

expressions.description: Expressions, all of which must match.

rules.description: Rules that decide when the action runs. The action runs when any rule matches. A rule matches when all of its expressions match. Without rules, the action always runs. Token actions can test the `application` (an application ID) and `grantType` fields. Password and profile actions can test the `flow` field, for example `adminInitiatedPasswordReset` or `userInitiatedPasswordUpdate`.

type.description: `pre_issue_access_token`, `pre_issue_id_token`, `pre_update_password`, `pre_update_profile` or `pre_registration` (the last needs to be enabled on the server). Changing it replaces the action.

block.description: Manages an action. An action is an HTTPS endpoint that you run, and that WSO2 Identity Server calls at a fixed point in a flow. For example, the server can call an action before it issues an access token or an ID token, so that the action can add or change claims. Other actions run before a password update, before a profile update, or before registration. By default, a tenant can have one action of each type. To import an action, use the ID `<type>/<id>`.

enabled.description: Show the banner.

block.description: Manages the advisory banner on the Console sign-in page. The resource only changes the settings that you set. Other settings keep their current values. When you destroy this resource, the settings keep their current values, and Terraform stops managing them. Each tenant (or organization) has one set of these settings. To import them, use the ID `admin_advisory_banner`.

schema.description: JSON Schema the authorization details must match (use `jsonencode`).

authorization_details_types.description: Rich authorization request (RFC 9396) types accepted by the API.

identifier.description: Unique identifier, usually the API's base URL (it becomes the `aud` of tokens). Changing it replaces the API resource.

requires_authorization.description: Whether applications must be authorized for the API before they can request its scopes. The server only accepts this value at creation. The default is `true`.

name.description: Scope name, as requested by applications, for example `orders:read`.

scopes.description: Scopes of the API. Scope names must be unique across the tenant. Changes replace the whole scope set on the server.

type.description: The type of the API resource. APIs that you create with this resource have the type `BUSINESS`.

block.description: Manages an API resource and its scopes. An API resource represents one of your APIs, and each scope is one permission in that API, such as `orders:read`. Use `wso2is_application_authorized_api` to let an application request the scopes, and `wso2is_role` to grant the scopes to users. To import an API resource, use its ID.

access.description: What the provider's user may do with this application. The value is `READ` for read-only system applications, and `WRITE` otherwise.

access_url.description: URL users open to reach the application (shown in My Account for discoverable applications).

android_attestation_service_credentials.description: The Google Play Integrity service account credentials, as JSON. The server never returns this value.

enabled.description: Require client attestation. The default is `false`.

value.description: PEM certificate, or the JWKS endpoint URL.

certificate.description: Application certificate used to validate signed requests and encrypt tokens.

discoverable_by_end_users.description: Whether the application is listed in My Account. The default is `false`.

user_store.description: User store domain of the groups, for example `PRIMARY`.

discoverable_groups.description: Groups whose members can discover the application in My Account. Empty means everyone.

enable_api_based_authentication.description: Allow app-native (API based) authentication. The default is `false`.

enable_authorization.description: Engage authorization policies during authentication. The default is `false`.

fragment.description: Whether this is a fragment (shared) application created by organization sharing.

return_authenticated_idp_list.description: Return the authenticated identity providers to the application. The default is `false`.

saas.description: Whether users of every tenant can sign in (super tenant only). The default is `false`.

skip_login_consent.description: Skip the attribute consent page at login. The default is `false`.

skip_logout_consent.description: Skip the logout confirmation page. The default is `false`.

is_consent_granted.description: Whether consent to publish the app details is granted. The default is `false`.

is_fido_trusted_app.description: Whether the app is a FIDO trusted app. The default is `false`.

trusted_app.description: Trusted (FIDO) application settings for passkeys in native apps.

use_external_consent_page.description: Use an external consent page. The default is `false`.

application_version.description: Version of the application model on the server.

allowed_audience.description: Which roles the application uses. With `APPLICATION`, the application only uses roles that were created for it. With `ORGANIZATION`, it uses the organization's roles. New applications use `APPLICATION` by default.

role_ids.description: The IDs of the roles that the application uses. Set this list when `allowed_audience = "ORGANIZATION"`. When `allowed_audience = "APPLICATION"`, the list is read-only and shows the roles that `wso2is_role` created for the application.

associated_roles.description: Which roles the application's users can be assigned and receive in tokens.

attribute_step_id.description: Step (1-based) whose user attributes are used.

request_path_authenticators.description: Request path authenticators, for example `BasicAuthRequestPathAuthenticator` or `OAuthRequestPathAuthenticator`.

authenticator.description: Authenticator name, for example `BasicAuthenticator`, `totp`, `email-otp-authenticator`, `sms-otp-authenticator`, `FIDOAuthenticator`, `MagicLinkAuthenticator`, or a federated authenticator such as `GoogleOIDCAuthenticator` or `OpenIDConnectAuthenticator`.

idp.description: `LOCAL` for local authenticators, otherwise the identity provider (connection) name.

options.description: Authenticators offered in this step (the login page shows them in the server's order).

steps.description: Authentication steps, in order. Each step lets the user choose one of its options.

subject_step_id.description: Step (1-based) whose user identity is used as the subject.

type.description: `DEFAULT` uses the tenant's default flow (username and password). `USER_DEFINED` uses `steps` and `script`. Set automatically to `USER_DEFINED` when `steps` or `script` are configured.

authentication_sequence.description: The login flow. It holds the authentication steps and an optional adaptive (conditional) authentication script. If you remove this block, the current flow stays as it is. To go back to the default flow, set `type = "DEFAULT"`.

claim_mappings.description: Maps the application's claim names to local claims. The `CUSTOM` dialect needs these mappings. With the `LOCAL` dialect, the server creates them from `requested_claims`.

dialect.description: `LOCAL` (use local claim URIs) or `CUSTOM` (map application claim names with `claim_mappings`).

mandatory.description: Whether the user must provide a value before signing in. The default is `false`.

requested_claims.description: The claims that the server shares with the application. With the `LOCAL` dialect, use local claim URIs (`http://wso2.org/claims/...`). With the `CUSTOM` dialect, use the application's claim names from `claim_mappings`.

claim.description: Claim carrying roles. The default is `http://wso2.org/claims/role`.

include_user_domain.description: Prefix role names with the user store domain. The default is `true`.

application_role.description: Role name sent to the application.

mappings.description: Local role to application role name mappings.

role.description: How roles are sent to the application.

claim.description: Local claim used as the subject. The default is `http://wso2.org/claims/userid`.

include_tenant_domain.description: Suffix the subject with the tenant domain. The default is `false`.

include_user_domain.description: Prefix the subject with the user store domain. The default is `false`.

mapped_local_subject_mandatory.description: Fail federated logins that have no mapped local user. The default is `false`.

use_mapped_local_subject.description: Use the local user mapped to a federated user as the subject. The server turns it on when the application is shared with organizations.

subject.description: How the subject identifier is built.

claim_configuration.description: User attributes (claims) the application requests and how the subject and roles are sent.

client_id.description: OAuth2 client ID, when OpenID Connect is configured.

enabled.description: Whether users can sign in to the application. The default is `true`.

enhanced_org_authentication_enabled.description: Whether enhanced organization authentication is enabled (organization login uses the organization's own login settings).

is_b2b_self_service_app.description: Whether the application is a B2B self-service application. The server only accepts this value when it creates the application, so changing it replaces the application.

is_management_app.description: Whether the application can call the management (system) APIs. The server only accepts this value when it creates the application, so changing it replaces the application.

issuer.description: SAML issuer, when SAML is configured.

logout_return_url.description: The URL that users go to after they log out, when the application does not send one. When you clear this value, the server stores `.*`, which allows any URL. The provider shows `.*` as unset.

access_token_attributes.description: User attributes (claim names) included in JWT access tokens.

application_access_token_expiry_in_secon.description: Lifetime of tokens issued to the application (client credentials).

enable_jwt_scope_as_array.description: Send the `scope` claim of JWT access tokens as an array. The default is `false`.

revoke_tokens_when_idp_session_terminate.description: Revoke tokens when the user's login session ends. The default is `false`.

user_access_token_expiry_in_seconds.description: Lifetime of tokens issued to users.

validate_token_binding.description: Validate the token binding on API calls. The default is `false`.

allowed_origins.description: Origins allowed to call the OAuth2 endpoints from browsers (CORS).

callback_urls.description: Authorized redirect URIs. A single value may be a regular expression prefixed with `regexp=`, for example `regexp=(https://a.example.com/cb|https://b.example.com/cb)`.

allow_federated_users.description: Allow notifications to users not in the local user store. The default is `false`.

skip_user_validation.description: Skip validating that the authenticated user matches `login_hint`. The default is `false`.

token_endpoint_allow_reuse_pvt_key_jwt.description: Allow reusing a private key JWT (only with `private_key_jwt`). The default is `false`.

client_id.description: The OAuth2 client ID. The server generates one when you do not set it. You can only choose the client ID when the application is created, so changing it replaces the application.

client_secret.description: Client secret. Generated when not set (empty for public clients). WSO2 only accepts a custom secret at creation, so changing it replaces the application.

enabled.description: Allow the hybrid flow. The default is `false`.

response_type.description: Comma separated allowed response types, for example `code id_token`.

enabled.description: Encrypt ID tokens (needs an application certificate). The default is `false`.

is_fapi_application.description: Make the application FAPI conformant. The server only accepts this value at creation.

logout.description: OIDC logout endpoints of the application.

support_plain_transform_algorithm.description: Accept the `plain` code challenge method. The default is `false`.

public_client.description: Allow the client to authenticate without a secret (single page and mobile apps). WSO2 still generates a client secret, which public clients do not use. The default is `false`.

extend_renewed_refresh_token_expiry_time.description: Give renewed refresh tokens a full new lifetime. When not set, the server derives it from `renew_refresh_token`.

renew_refresh_token.description: Issue a new refresh token on every refresh.

require_pushed_authorization_requests.description: Only accept authorization requests sent through PAR. The default is `false`.

scope_validators.description: Scope validators, for example `Role based scope validator`.

sector_identifier_uri.description: Sector identifier URI for pairwise subjects.

enabled.description: Issue subject tokens. The default is `false`.

subject_token.description: Subject token issuance for token exchange (impersonation).

token_issuer_organization_id.description: The organization whose issuer signs the tokens. This setting only applies to applications inside an organization, that is, with a provider that sets `organization_id`. By default, the root organization signs the tokens. To make the application's own organization the issuer, set its organization ID. In the root organization, the value is `""`.

validate_request_object_signature.description: Require signed request objects. The default is `false`.

oidc.description: OpenID Connect / OAuth2 configuration. Remove the attribute to remove the protocol from the application.

reply_to_logout.description: URL users return to after logout.

passive_sts.description: WS-Federation (passive STS) configuration. Remove the attribute to remove the protocol.

provisioning_userstore_domain.description: User store that receives provisioned users (when not in proxy mode).

proxy_mode.description: Forward provisioning requests to outbound connectors without storing users locally. The default is `false`.

inbound.description: Users and groups provisioned through SCIM by this application.

connector.description: Outbound provisioning connector name, for example `scim2`, `googleapps`, `salesforce`.

outbound_identity_providers.description: Identity providers users are provisioned to.

always_include_attributes_in_response.description: Include attributes even when not requested. The default is `false`.

enabled.description: Include an attribute statement. The default is `false`.

default_assertion_consumer_url.description: Default ACS URL. The default is the first of `assertion_consumer_urls`.

enable_assertion_query_profile.description: Enable the assertion query/request profile. The default is `false`.

idp_entity_id_alias.description: IdP entity ID used for this service provider. The default is the resident IdP entity ID.

issuer.description: SAML issuer (entity ID) of the service provider.

metadata_url.description: Service provider metadata URL. The server reads issuer, ACS URLs and certificates from it when the protocol is configured.

signature_validation_cert_alias.description: Alias of the certificate used to validate request signatures.

enabled.description: Sign SAML responses.

service_provider_qualifier.description: Qualifier to allow several service providers with the same issuer.

enabled.description: Enable single logout. The default is `false`.
Allow IdP initiated logout. The default is `false`.
Encrypt assertions (needs the service provider certificate). The default is `false`.

attribute_consuming_service_index.description: Attribute consuming service index assigned by the server.

enable_idp_initiated_single_sign_on.description: Allow IdP initiated SSO. The default is `false`.

enable_signature_validation_for_artifact.description: Validate signatures of artifact resolve requests. The default is `false`.

saml.description: SAML 2.0 web SSO configuration. Either configure it manually (`issuer` and `assertion_consumer_urls`) or point to the service provider metadata with `metadata_url`. Remove the attribute to remove the protocol.

template_id.description: The Console template that the application was created from, for example `custom-application`, `m2m-application`, `single-page-application`, `oidc-web-application` or `react-application`. The template only changes how the Console shows the application.

audience.description: Audience (endpoint address) of the trusted service.

certificate_alias.description: Alias of the service's certificate in the tenant keystore.

ws_trust.description: WS-Trust configuration (needs the WS-Trust connector installed on the server). Remove the attribute to remove the protocol.

block.description:
Manages an application, which the server also calls a service provider. The resource covers the application's sign-in protocols (OpenID Connect and OAuth2, SAML 2.0, WS-Federation and WS-Trust), its login flow, the user attributes that it requests, its roles and its advanced settings.

If you leave out a setting, the server uses its default value, and the provider shows that value in the state. If you later remove a setting from the configuration, the setting keeps its last value. To change it, set the new value explicitly.

Manage the API scopes that the application may request with `wso2is_application_authorized_api`. Share the application with sub-organizations with `wso2is_application_share`. To import an application, use its ID.

authorization_details_types.description: Authorization details types the application may request. Changing them replaces the authorization.

policy_identifier.description: The authorization policy. With `RBAC`, users get the scopes that their roles grant. With `No Policy`, every signed-in user gets the authorized scopes. The default is `RBAC`.

scopes.description: Scope names the application may request.

block.description: Allows an application to request the scopes of an API resource. In the Console, this is the application's **API Authorization** tab. Use it for your own APIs (`wso2is_api_resource`) and for the server's management APIs. To find a management API, use the `wso2is_api_resource` data source. For example, you can allow an M2M application to call the user management API. To import, use the ID `<application_id>/<api_resource_id>`.

organization_ids.description: IDs of the organizations to share the application with.

share_with_all_children.description: Share with every current and future child organization. Conflicts with `organization_ids`.

block.description: Shares an application with sub-organizations. Users of those organizations can then sign in to the application, and each organization gets its own copy of it. The resource manages the complete list of organizations that the application is shared with. To import, use the application ID.

preference.description: Branding preference document (use `jsonencode`), as in the Console's *Branding* section: `configs` (`isBrandingEnabled`, `removeDefaultBranding`, `selfSignUpEnabled`), `organizationDetails` (`displayName`, `supportEmail`, `siteTitle`, `copyrightText`), `images` (`logo`, `favicon`, `myAccountLogo`), `urls` (`privacyPolicyURL`, `termsOfUseURL`, `cookiePolicyURL`), `theme` (`activeTheme`, `LIGHT`/`DARK` colors, fonts, buttons, inputs, `loginBox`, `footer`), and `layout` (`activeLayout`: `centered`, `left-image`, `right-aligned`, `custom`, ...). The server stores the document as given.

block.description: Manages the branding of the login, registration, account recovery and My Account pages. The branding applies to the whole organization or to one application. To import, use the ID `ORG/<tenant>/<locale>` or `APP/<application_id>/<locale>`.

screen.description: Screen whose texts are customized, for example `common`, `login`, `sign-up`, `password-recovery`, `password-reset`, `password-reset-success`, `email-otp`, `sms-otp`, `totp`, `email-link-expiry`, `myaccount`.

text.description: Text values by key, for example `{ "login.heading" = "Sign in to Acme" }`. The keys are listed in the Console's *Text* tab of the branding section.

block.description: Changes the text on one login or self-service screen, in one language (locale). The text applies to the whole organization or to one application. To import, use the ID `ORG/<tenant>/<locale>/<screen>` or `APP/<application_id>/<locale>/<screen>`.

attribute_mappings.description: User store attribute (column or LDAP attribute) by user store domain, for example `{ PRIMARY = "employeeId" }`.

claim_uri.description: Claim URI, for example `http://wso2.org/claims/employeeId`. Changing it replaces the claim.

display_name.description: Name shown in forms and the Console.

display_order.description: Position of the attribute in profile and registration forms. The default is `0`.

excluded_user_stores.description: User stores where the attribute is not available.

id.description: Claim ID (base64url of the claim URI).

input_type.description: Input control used in forms, for example `text_input`, `dropdown`, `checkbox_group`, `radio_group`, `date_picker`, `toggle`.

managed_in_user_store.description: Whether the value is stored in the user store (otherwise in the identity database).

multi_valued.description: The attribute holds several values. The default is `false`.

read_only.description: Users cannot change the value in this profile.

profiles.description: Per-profile overrides (WSO2 IS 7.1+), keyed by profile: `console`, `endUser`, `selfRegistration`.

properties.description: Additional claim properties. Only the keys listed here are managed.

read_only.description: Users cannot change the value. The default is `false`.

required.description: A value is mandatory in profiles. The default is `false`.

shared_profile_value_resolving_method.description: How the value is resolved for users shared with sub-organizations: `FromOrigin`, `FromSharedProfile` or `FromFirstFoundInHierarchy`.

sub_attributes.description: Sub-attribute claim URIs of a `complex` attribute.

supported_by_default.description: Shown in user profiles (and self registration) by default. The default is `false`.

block.description:
Manages a local claim. A local claim is a user attribute in the `http://wso2.org/claims` dialect. The resource also sets where each user store keeps the attribute.

Applications do not see local claims directly. To send the attribute to applications, map it in the OIDC dialect with `wso2is_external_claim` (`dialect_uri = "http://wso2.org/oidc/claim"`), and add it to an OIDC scope with `wso2is_oidc_scope`. To show it in the SCIM APIs, map it in a SCIM dialect too. To import a claim, use its claim URI.

dialect_uri.description: Dialect URI, for example `urn:example:claims`. Changing it replaces the dialect.

block.description: Manages an external claim dialect. A dialect is a set of claim URIs that another system uses, such as an identity provider or an older application. Map each claim of the dialect to a local claim with `wso2is_external_claim`. Deleting a dialect also deletes its claims. To import a dialect, use its dialect URI.

allow_subdomains.description: Allow subdomains of the allowed origins.

max_age.description: Preflight cache lifetime in seconds (`-1` = not set).

supported_headers.description: Request headers allowed when `support_any_header` is off.

supported_methods.description: HTTP methods allowed in CORS requests.

block.description: Manages the CORS settings of the server's endpoints. The allowed origins come from the `oidc.allowed_origins` setting of each application. The resource only changes the settings that you set. Other settings keep their current values. When you destroy this resource, the settings keep their current values, and Terraform stops managing them. Each tenant (or organization) has one set of these settings. To import them, use the ID `cors_configuration`.

authentication_type.description: `IDENTIFICATION` (the service identifies the user, for a first step) or `VERIFICATION` (it verifies an already identified user, for later steps). Changing it replaces the authenticator.

display_name.description: Name shown on the login page.

enabled.description: Whether the authenticator can be used. The default is `true`.

endpoint_authentication_properties.description: The credentials for the service. Use `username` and `password`, `accessToken`, or `header` and `value`, to match `endpoint_authentication_type`. The server never returns these values.

endpoint_authentication_type.description: How WSO2 signs in to the service. The allowed values are `NONE`, `BASIC`, `BEARER` and `API_KEY`.

endpoint_uri.description: HTTPS endpoint of the authentication service.

name.description: The authenticator name. It must start with `custom-`. Changing the name replaces the authenticator.

block.description: Manages a custom local authenticator (WSO2 IS 7.1 and later). A custom authenticator is a login step that your own HTTPS service performs, and that WSO2 calls during login. To use it, add it to an application's `authentication_sequence` with `idp = "LOCAL"` and `authenticator = <name>`. Custom federated authenticators work differently: you set them up on `wso2is_identity_provider` with an endpoint. To import, use the authenticator name.

enable_fapi_enforcement.description: Enforce FAPI rules on registered clients.

ssa_jwks.description: JWKS URL used to validate software statement assertions.

block.description: Manages OAuth2 dynamic client registration (`/api/identity/oauth2/dcr/v1.1/register`). The resource only changes the settings that you set. Other settings keep their current values. When you destroy this resource, the settings keep their current values, and Terraform stops managing them. Each tenant (or organization) has one set of these settings. To import them, use the ID `dcr_configuration`.

auth_type.description: How the server signs in to the email provider. `BASIC` is the default and uses `username` and `password`. `CLIENT_CREDENTIAL` uses the `clientId`, `clientSecret`, `tokenEndpoint` and `scopes` properties. `BEARER` uses `accessToken`. `API_KEY` is for HTTP providers. `NONE` sends no credentials.

display_name.description: Sender name shown to recipients (`mail.smtp.signature`). SMTP providers need this value.

password.description: Password for `BASIC` authentication. The server never returns this value.

properties.description: Additional properties, for example `mail.smtp.starttls.enable`, `mail.smtp.auth`, or for HTTP providers `body`, `http.client.method`, `contentType`, `http.headers`. Only the keys listed are managed.

provider_type.description: The kind of email provider. `SMTP` is the default. With `HTTP` (WSO2 IS 7.3 and later), the server posts each email to `provider_url`.

provider_url.description: Endpoint of an HTTP email provider. Set the request template in `properties.body`.

reply_to.description: Reply-to address (`mail.smtp.replyTo`). SMTP providers need this value.

secret_properties.description: Confidential properties such as `clientSecret` or `accessToken`. The server never returns this value.

block.description:
Manages the tenant's email provider. In the Console, this is **Notification Channels > Email Provider**. The server uses it to send verification, account recovery, one-time password and notification emails. Each tenant has one email provider.

This resource does not work in the super tenant (`carbon.super`). The super tenant reads its email provider only from `deployment.toml` (`[output_adapter.email]`), and the API answers HTTP 405. Use this resource with a provider that manages another tenant. To import, use the ID `EmailPublisher`.

claim_uri.description: External claim URI, for example `employee_id` (OIDC) or `urn:scim:schemas:extension:custom:User:employeeId` (SCIM). Changing it replaces the claim.

dialect_uri.description: Dialect URI. Changing it replaces the claim.

mapped_local_claim_uri.description: Local claim URI it maps to.

block.description:
Maps a claim of an external dialect to a local claim. You can also use the built-in dialects:

* `http://wso2.org/oidc/claim` holds the OIDC claims. Add them to tokens with `wso2is_oidc_scope`.
* `urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User`, `urn:scim:wso2:schema` and `urn:scim:schemas:extension:custom:User` hold SCIM attributes.

A new server has no custom SCIM dialect. The provider creates it when you add the first claim to it, and leaves it in place when you destroy the resource. To import, use the ID `<dialect_uri>|<claim_uri>`.

completion_configs.description: Settings that apply when the flow finishes, for example `isEmailVerificationEnabled`, `isAutoLoginEnabled`, `isAccountLockOnCreationEnabled` and `isFlowCompletionNotificationEnabled`. The values are the strings `"true"` and `"false"`. The provider only manages the keys that you list.

enabled.description: Whether the flow replaces the older, built-in flow. For registration, this means that the flow builds the self sign-up page. The default is `true`.

steps.description: The steps of the flow, as a JSON array. Each step has an `id`, a `type` (such as `VIEW`, `REDIRECTION` or `END`), a `size` and a `position` (its place in the Console's editor), and `data`. The `data.components` list holds the step's content: `TYPOGRAPHY` text, and `FORM` blocks with `INPUT` fields and `BUTTON`s. Each field's `config.identifier` is a claim URI, or `password` or `otp`. Each button has an `action`, for example `{ type = "EXECUTOR", executor = { name = ... }, next = <step id or "END"> }`. The last step is `{ id = "END", type = "END" }`.

block.description:
Manages a flow that the Console's flow builder can also edit (WSO2 IS 7.2 and later). A flow is the self sign-up form and its steps, the password recovery flow, or the invited user registration flow. Use this resource to build a custom sign-up form.

In a flow, form fields map to claims, and executors do the work of each step. Examples of executors are `PasswordProvisioningExecutor`, `EmailOTPExecutor`, `UserProvisioningExecutor` and federated executors such as `GoogleExecutor`.

`steps` holds the same JSON document that the Console stores (`GET /api/server/v1/flow?flowType=...`). You can design the flow in the Console and copy it with the `wso2is_flow` data source, or write it with `jsonencode`.

When you destroy the resource, the provider turns the flow off and deletes it. By default, WSO2 IS 7.3.0 does not allow the API to delete the root organization's flow. In that case, the provider only turns the flow off. The server behaviour guide explains how to allow deletion. To import a flow, use its flow type.

log_request_payload.description: Log the payload sent to the fraud detection service.

block.description: Manages how the server sends events to a fraud detection service. The resource only changes the settings that you set. Other settings keep their current values. When you destroy this resource, the settings keep their current values, and Terraform stops managing them. Each tenant (or organization) has one set of these settings. To import them, use the ID `fraud_detection_configuration`.

properties.description: Property values by property name, for example `{ "account.lock.handler.lock.on.max.failed.attempts.enable" = "true" }`. Values are strings.

restore_on_destroy.description: Revert the managed properties to the server defaults when the resource is destroyed. The default is `true`.

block.description:
Manages an identity governance connector. Governance connectors hold the tenant-wide login, registration, account recovery and account policies. In the Console, they are under **Login & Registration**.

The resource only manages the properties that you list. If you remove a property from the configuration, the provider sets it back to the server default. When you destroy the resource, the provider sets all listed properties back to their defaults, unless `restore_on_destroy = false`.

Examples of connectors are `account.lock.handler`, `account.disable.handler`, `self-sign-up`, `lite-user-sign-up`, `user-email-verification`, `account-recovery`, `admin-forced-password-reset`, `passwordHistory`, `passwordExpiry`, `multiattribute.login.handler`, `sso.login.recaptcha`, `suspension.notification`, `pii-controller`, `user-claim-update` and `organization-self-service`. MFA connectors include `email-otp-authenticator`, `sms-otp-authenticator`, `totp`, `backup-code-authenticator` and `FIDOAuthenticator`. To see a connector's properties, use the `wso2is_governance_connector` data source. To import, use the connector name.

name.description: Group name, without the user store prefix.

user_store.description: User store domain. The default is `PRIMARY`. Changing it replaces the group.

block.description: Manages a group of users. Manage the members with `wso2is_group_members`, and the roles with `wso2is_role_assignment`. By default, the server requires group names to be 3 to 30 characters long, without spaces. To import a group, use its ID.
Manages the complete list of members of a group. The provider removes any user who is not in the list. Use only one `wso2is_group_members` for each group. To import, use the group ID.

alias.description: Alias used as the audience of tokens this provider issues (for example the token endpoint of the resident IdP).

certificates.description: PEM certificates of the provider (for validating signed responses and tokens). Conflicts with `jwks_uri`.

idp_claim.description: Claim name used by the provider.

mappings.description: Provider claim to local claim mappings. Without mappings the provider's claims are used as is.

provisioning_claims.description: Default values of claims for outbound provisioning.

user_id_claim.description: The identity provider's claim that identifies the user. When it is empty, the server uses the subject.

claims.description: Claim mappings from the provider's attributes to local claims.

default_authenticator.description: Name of the federated authenticator used by default. The default is the only (or first) configured authenticator.

default_outbound_connector.description: Name of the default outbound provisioning connector.

enabled.description: Whether the connection can be used. The default is `true`.
Whether the authenticator is enabled. The default is `true`.

authentication_properties.description: Credentials: `username`/`password` (BASIC), `accessToken` (BEARER) or `header`/`value` (API_KEY). The server never returns this value.

endpoint.description: External service endpoint of a custom (user defined) federated authenticator.

federated_authenticators.description: Federated authenticators, keyed by authenticator name: `GoogleOIDCAuthenticator`, `GithubAuthenticator`, `FacebookAuthenticator`, `MicrosoftWindowsLiveAuthenticator`, `Office365Authenticator`, `AppleOIDCAuthenticator`, `TwitterAuthenticator`, `OpenIDConnectAuthenticator`, `SAMLSSOAuthenticator`, `PassiveSTSAuthenticator`, `IWAKerberosAuthenticator`, `EmailOTP`, `SMSOTP`, or a custom authenticator.

force_delete.description: Delete the connection even when applications still use it. The default is `false`.

groups.description: Groups defined at the provider that can be mapped to local roles.

home_realm_identifier.description: Home realm identifier (`fidp` request parameter value) that selects this provider.

idp_issuer_name.description: Issuer of tokens from this provider, when different from its name (used to validate JWT bearer grants).

enabled.description: Enable implicit association. The default is `false`.

lookup_attributes.description: Local claim URIs used to find the local user.

implicit_association.description: Associate federated users with local users that have matching attributes.

is_federation_hub.description: The provider is a federation hub (it fronts other providers). The default is `false`.

is_primary.description: Use as the primary (default) identity provider. The default is `false`.

account_lookup_attribute_mappings.description: Local and federated attributes used to find an existing local user.

associate_local_user.description: Link to an existing local user found through the lookup attributes. The default is `false`.

enabled.description: Create local users on first login. The default is `false`.

skip_jit_for_lookup_failure.description: Skip provisioning when the local user lookup fails. The default is `false`.

user_store.description: User store for provisioned users. The default is `PRIMARY`.

jit_provisioning.description: Just-in-time provisioning of local accounts for federated users.

jwks_uri.description: JWKS endpoint used to validate tokens signed by the provider. Conflicts with `certificates`.

name.description: Unique name, used in authentication steps.

enabled.description: Enabled. The default is `true`.

outbound_provisioning_connectors.description: Outbound provisioning connectors keyed by name: `SCIM2`, `scim`, `googleapps`, `salesforce`.

outbound_provisioning_roles.description: Only users with these roles are provisioned to this provider.

idp_role.description: Role name sent by the provider.

local_role.description: Local role, as `Internal/<role name>` for organization roles (WSO2 silently ignores other formats).

role_mappings.description: Provider role to local role mappings.

template_id.description: The Console template, for example `google-idp`, `github-idp`, `enterprise-oidc-idp` or `enterprise-saml-idp`. The template only changes how the Console shows the connection. The server only accepts it at creation, so changing it replaces the connection.

block.description:
Manages an identity provider, which the Console calls a connection. An identity provider lets users sign in with another system. Examples are social logins (Google, GitHub, Facebook, Microsoft and Apple) and any OpenID Connect or SAML provider. The resource also manages claim and role mappings, just-in-time provisioning and outbound provisioning.

Authenticator and connector settings are properties with the names that the server uses. The `wso2is_federated_authenticator_metadata` data source lists them. The provider only manages the property keys that you set. Put secrets in `secret_properties`, so that plans hide them. To use the identity provider for login, add it to an application's `authentication_sequence`. To import, use the identity provider's ID.

claim_mappings.description: Provider claim by local claim URI, for example `{ "http://wso2.org/claims/givenname" = "first_name" }`.

enabled.description: Whether the provider is enabled. The default is `true`.

image_url.description: Logo URL. The server sets a default for known types.

properties.description: Configuration properties, for example `base_url` and `workflow_id` for Onfido.

secret_properties.description: Confidential configuration properties, for example `token` and `webhook_token` for Onfido.

type.description: Provider type, for example `ONFIDO` (the connector must be installed). Changing it replaces the provider.

block.description: Manages an identity verification provider, such as Onfido. The server uses it to check users' identity documents. To import, use the provider's ID.

enable_email_notification.description: Email users when they are impersonated.

block.description: Manages the user impersonation settings. The resource only changes the settings that you set. Other settings keep their current values. When you destroy this resource, the provider restores the server defaults. Each tenant (or organization) has one set of these settings. To import them, use the ID `impersonation_configuration`.

provisioning_userstore.description: The user store that receives every user created through `/scim2`. The default, `""`, lets the `DOMAIN/` prefix of each username choose the user store. **When you set a user store, the server ignores the user store of new users, including `wso2is_user.user_store`. It also refuses SCIM updates of users in other user stores.**

proxy_mode.description: Forward SCIM provisioning requests to outbound connectors without storing users locally.

block.description: Manages inbound SCIM provisioning for requests that sign in with basic authentication (the resident service provider). Requests that use an application's OAuth2 token follow that application's own provisioning settings instead. The resource only changes the settings that you set. Other settings keep their current values. When you destroy this resource, the provider restores the server defaults. Each tenant (or organization) has one set of these settings. To import them, use the ID `inbound_provisioning_configuration`.

enable_token_reuse.description: Allow a client assertion JWT (same `jti`) to be used more than once.

block.description: Manages how the server checks JWTs that clients use as client assertions (`private_key_jwt`). The resource only changes the settings that you set. Other settings keep their current values. When you destroy this resource, the settings keep their current values, and Terraform stops managing them. Each tenant (or organization) has one set of these settings. To import them, use the ID `jwt_key_validator_configuration`.

application_id.description: The ID of the application that this template is for. When it is not set, the template is the organization's template.

content_type.description: Email content type. The default is `text/html`.

locale.description: Locale such as `en_US` or `fr_FR`. The default is `en_US`.

block.description:
Customizes an email or SMS notification template in one language (locale). The template applies to the whole organization or to one application. When you destroy the resource, the server goes back to the system template.

Templates use placeholders, such as `{{user-name}}`, `{{confirmation-code}}`, `{{organization-name}}` and `{{ url:...}}`. Template types include `AccountConfirmation`, `AskPassword`, `PasswordReset`, `passwordResetSucess`, `ResendAccountConfirmation`, `EmailOTP`, `SMSOTP`, `AccountLockFailedAttempt`, `AccountUnlockAdmin`, `AccountDisable`, `OrganizationUserInvitation`, `magicLink` and `TemporaryPassword`. You can also use your own types from `wso2is_notification_template_type`. To import, use the ID `<channel>/<type>/<locale>` or `<channel>/<type>/<locale>/<application_id>`.

Creates a custom notification template type. Use a custom type for notifications that your own flows or adaptive scripts send. Deleting the type also deletes its templates. To import, use the ID `<channel>/<name>`.

enable_jwt_scope_as_array.description: Send the `scope` claim of JWT access tokens as an array (applications can override it).

block.description: Manages the tenant-wide OAuth2 settings. The resource only changes the settings that you set. Other settings keep their current values. When you destroy this resource, the provider restores the server defaults. Each tenant (or organization) has one set of these settings. To import them, use the ID `oauth2_configuration`.

Manages which organizations may use the root organization's token issuer. The resource only changes the settings that you set. Other settings keep their current values. When you destroy this resource, the settings keep their current values, and Terraform stops managing them. Each tenant (or organization) has one set of these settings. To import them, use the ID `oauth2_issuer_usage_scope`.

claims.description: OIDC claim names, for example `email`, `given_name`, or custom ones mapped with `wso2is_external_claim`.

display_name.description: Display name shown on consent pages.

name.description: Scope name. Changing it replaces the scope.

block.description: Manages an OpenID Connect scope. When an application requests the scope, the server returns the scope's OIDC claims in ID tokens and from the `/userinfo` endpoint. The claims must exist in the `http://wso2.org/oidc/claim` dialect. You can also import and change the built-in scopes, such as `openid`, `profile`, `email`, `phone` and `address`. To import, use the scope name.

enabled.description: Whether the organization is active. The default is `true`.

handle.description: Organization handle (used in URLs, WSO2 IS 7.1+). The default is the server's choice (the ID). The server only accepts this value at creation.

parent_id.description: The ID of the parent organization, which is the organization that the provider manages. WSO2 only creates an organization from its parent. To create a nested organization, use a provider alias whose `organization_id` is the parent.

type.description: `TENANT` (default) or `STRUCTURAL`. The server only accepts this value at creation.

block.description: Manages a sub-organization (a B2B organization). The organization sits under the root organization or under another sub-organization. Share applications with it with `wso2is_application_share`. To manage objects inside it, add a provider block with an `alias` that sets `organization_id`. The server only deletes an organization after its child organizations. To import, use the organization ID.

email_domains.description: Email domains of the organization's users, for example `partner.example`. A domain can belong to one organization only.

block.description: Sets the email domains of a sub-organization's users, for email domain discovery. The login page then sends users with these domains to the organization. Turn on email domain discovery first with `wso2is_organization_discovery_configuration`, or the server answers `ORG-60080`. Add `depends_on` for that resource, so that Terraform also removes the domains before it turns discovery off. Manage this resource from the root organization. To import, use the organization ID.

default_param.description: What users type when they choose their organization on the login page, either `orgHandle` or `orgName`. When it is not set, the server uses its default.

email_domain_based_self_sign_up_enabled.description: Let users self-register in the organization that owns their email domain. The default is `false`.

email_domain_enabled.description: Discover the organization from the user's email domain.

block.description: Turns on organization discovery for the root organization. With discovery on, the login page sends users to their organization's login, based on the domain of their email address. Set each organization's domains with `wso2is_organization_discovery`. Each tenant has one configuration. When you destroy the resource, the provider removes the configuration, which turns discovery off. To import, use the ID `organization_discovery_configuration`.

Manages the WS-Federation (passive STS) endpoint. The resource only changes the settings that you set. Other settings keep their current values. When you destroy this resource, the provider restores the server defaults. Each tenant (or organization) has one set of these settings. To import them, use the ID `passive_sts_configuration`.

access_key_id.description: Access key ID of an IAM user allowed to manage SNS platform endpoints and publish.

platform_arns.description: Platform application ARN by platform, for example `{ FCM = "arn:aws:sns:...:app/GCM/my-app", APNS = "..." }`.

default.description: Use this provider for devices that do not name one when they register. The default is `false`.

service_account_json.description: Content of the Firebase service account key file (JSON), for example `file("service-account.json")`.

provider_name.description: `FCM` or `AmazonSNS`. Changing it replaces the sender.

block.description: Manages a push notification provider. In the Console, this is **Notification Channels > Push Providers**. The push notification authenticator uses it. WSO2 IS 7.3 supports Firebase Cloud Messaging and Amazon SNS, with one of each per tenant. The server returns the credentials in its API responses, so the credentials appear in the Terraform state. To import, use the ID `FCM_PushPublisher` or `AmazonSNS_PushPublisher`.

keystore_location.description: Path, on the server, of a keystore with a client certificate.

password.description: Basic authentication password (write-only on the server).

remote_url.description: Endpoint the logs are posted to.

truststore_location.description: Path, on the server, of a truststore for the endpoint's certificate.

verify_hostname.description: Verify the endpoint's hostname. The default is `true`.

block.description: Sends server logs (audit logs or carbon logs) to a remote HTTP endpoint. This resource only works in the super tenant. When you destroy the resource, the server stops sending the logs. To import, use the log type.

audience_id.description: Application ID for application roles. For organization roles it is computed (the organization ID). Changing it replaces the role.

audience_name.description: Name of the organization or application the role belongs to.

audience_type.description: `organization` (default) or `application`. Changing it replaces the role.

name.description: Role name, unique within its audience.

permissions.description: Scope names granted by the role. For application roles they must belong to APIs the application is authorized for.

shared.description: Whether the role is shared from a parent organization.

block.description: Manages a role and the API scopes (permissions) that it grants. A role belongs either to the organization or to one application. An application can only have its own roles when it sets `associated_roles.allowed_audience = "APPLICATION"`. Assign users and groups to the role with `wso2is_role_assignment`. To import a role, use its ID.

group_ids.description: IDs of groups assigned the role.

user_ids.description: IDs of users assigned the role.

block.description: Manages the complete list of users and groups that have a role. The provider removes any assignment that is not in the list. Use only one `wso2is_role_assignment` for each role. Every user also has the built-in `everyone` role, which this resource does not manage. To import, use the role ID.

destination_urls.description: SAML SSO endpoint URLs advertised to service providers.

metadata_validity_period.description: Validity of the published metadata, in minutes.

block.description: Manages the server's settings as a SAML identity provider, such as its metadata and destination URLs. The resource only changes the settings that you set. Other settings keep their current values. When you destroy this resource, the provider restores the server defaults. Each tenant (or organization) has one set of these settings. To import them, use the ID `saml_idp_configuration`.

name.description: The library name. It must end with `.js`. Changing the name replaces the library.

block.description: Manages a JavaScript library for adaptive authentication scripts. A script loads the library with `var lib = require('<name>');`. The library shares its functions through `module.exports`. To import, use the library name.

name.description: Secret name (letters, digits and underscores). Changing it replaces the secret.

type.description: Secret type. The default is `ADAPTIVE_AUTH_CALL_CHOREO`, the type adaptive scripts read.

value.description: The secret value. Terraform stores it in the state. Use `value_wo` instead to keep it out of the state.

value_wo.description: Write-only secret value (Terraform 1.11+). Change `value_wo_version` to update it.

value_wo_version.description: Increase this number to send a new `value_wo`.

block.description: Stores a secret for adaptive authentication scripts. Scripts read the secret as `secrets.<name>`, for example in `httpGet` or `httpPost` calls. The server never returns the value, so the provider cannot notice changes made outside Terraform. To import, use the ID `<type>/<name>`.

enable_maximum_session_timeout.description: End sessions after `maximum_session_timeout` regardless of activity.

home_realm_identifiers.description: Home realm identifiers of the resident identity provider.

preserve_current_session_at_password_upd.description: Keep the current session when the user changes their password (other sessions end).

remember_me_period.description: How long *Remember me* keeps users signed in, in minutes.

block.description: Manages the tenant-wide session and provisioning settings. In the Console, these settings are under **Login & Registration > Session** and in the resident identity provider. The resource only changes the settings that you set. Other settings keep their current values. When you destroy this resource, the settings keep their current values, and Terraform stops managing them. Each tenant (or organization) has one set of these settings. To import them, use the ID `server_configuration`.

authentication_properties.description: Authentication properties, for example `username`/`password` (BASIC), `accessToken` (BEARER), `header`/`value` (API_KEY), `clientId`/`clientSecret`/`tokenEndpoint`/`scopes`. The server never returns this value.

authentication_type.description: How the server signs in to a custom provider's endpoint. The allowed values are `BASIC`, `CLIENT_CREDENTIAL`, `BEARER`, `API_KEY` and `NONE`.

content_type.description: `JSON` or `FORM`, the format of requests to the provider.

key.description: Account key or ID (Twilio account SID, Vonage key). With BASIC authentication the server reports the username here.

properties.description: Additional properties, for example `body` (request template with `{{mobile}}` and `{{body}}` placeholders), `http.client.method`, `http.headers`.

block.description: Manages the tenant's SMS provider. In the Console, this is **Notification Channels > SMS Provider**. The server uses it for SMS one-time passwords and SMS notifications. Each tenant has one SMS provider. To import, use the ID `SMSPublisher`.

activated.description: Whether the tenant is active. Deactivated tenants cannot be used to sign in. The default is `true`.

domain.description: Tenant domain, for example `acme.com`. Changing it replaces the tenant.

name.description: Display name. The default is the domain. The server only accepts this value at creation.

owner_first_name.description: First name of the tenant owner.

owner_id.description: User ID of the tenant owner.

owner_last_name.description: Last name of the tenant owner.

owner_password.description: The tenant owner's password. The server never returns it, so the provider cannot notice changes made outside Terraform.

owner_username.description: Username of the tenant owner (without the domain). Changing it replaces the tenant.

block.description:
Manages a tenant (a root organization) and its owner.

The provider that creates the tenant must manage the super tenant (`tenant_domain = "carbon.super"`). It must use basic authentication, with a user who may manage tenants. With an application's client credentials, the server fails to create the tenant (`TM-65002`, "Error in adding claims to the user").

To manage objects inside the tenant, add another provider block with an `alias`. Set `tenant_domain = wso2is_tenant.<name>.domain`, and sign in as the owner (`username = "<owner>@<domain>"`). This works in the same configuration.

When you destroy the resource, the provider deletes the tenant if the server allows it (`[tenant_mgt] tenant_deletion = true` in `deployment.toml`). Otherwise, the provider deactivates the tenant and shows a warning. To import, use the tenant ID or domain.

ask_password.description: Create the user without a password and email them a link to set one (needs an email address and the Ask Password governance setting). The provider only uses this value when it creates the user.

attributes.description: Other SCIM attributes, by path. Core attributes use their name, such as `title`, `locale` or `name.middleName`. Extension attributes start with their schema URN, for example `urn:scim:wso2:schema:country`, `urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User:department` or `urn:scim:schemas:extension:custom:User:<custom claim>`. All values are strings. The provider converts booleans and numbers with the server's SCIM schema. Separate the values of a multi-valued attribute with commas.

disabled.description: Whether the account is disabled. This sets `urn:scim:wso2:schema:accountDisabled`, which needs the account disabling governance connector (`account.disable.handler`).

email.description: Primary email address (`http://wso2.org/claims/emailaddress`), used for notifications and account recovery.

emails.description: More email addresses, by type (`work`, `home` or `other`). For several verified addresses, use the `urn:scim:wso2:schema:emailAddresses` attribute instead.

locked.description: Whether the account is locked (`urn:scim:wso2:schema:accountLocked`). The server also locks the account after failed logins when account locking is on.

password.description: The user's password. It must meet the tenant's password policy. Terraform stores it in the state. Use `password_wo` instead to keep it out of the state.

password_wo.description: A write-only password (Terraform 1.11 or later). The provider sends it to the server but never stores it in the state. To set a new password, change it and increase `password_wo_version`.

password_wo_version.description: Increase this number to send a new `password_wo`.

user_store.description: User store domain. The default is `PRIMARY`. Changing it replaces the user.

username.description: Username, without the user store prefix. Changing it replaces the user (WSO2 does not support renaming).

block.description:
Manages a user through the SCIM 2.0 API.

The provider only manages the attributes in your configuration. It leaves alone the attributes that the user sets in My Account, or that other systems set.

The server never sends passwords back. As a result, the provider cannot notice a password that someone changed outside Terraform. Use `password_wo` (Terraform 1.11 or later) to keep the password out of the state, or `ask_password` to let the user choose a password. To import a user, use the user's ID.

include_children.description: Also share with the organization's current and future child organizations. `false` when omitted.

audience_name.description: Name of the application, or of the organization for organization roles.

audience_type.description: `application` for a role of a shared application, `organization` for an organization role.

roles.description: Roles the shared user gets in the organization(s). None when omitted.

organizations.description: Organizations to share the user with.

audience_name.description: Name of the application, or of the organization for organization roles.

audience_type.description: `application` for a role of a shared application, `organization` for an organization role.

roles.description: Roles the shared user gets in the organization(s). None when omitted.

share_with_all.description: Share with every current and future organization. Conflicts with `organizations`.

user_id.description: ID of a user of the root organization.

block.description: Shares a user of the root organization with sub-organizations (WSO2 IS 7.3 and later). The user can also get roles in those organizations. The same account can then sign in to the organizations' applications. The resource manages all shares of the user. The server applies changes in the background, and the provider waits until they are visible. To import, use the user ID.

claim_attribute_mappings.description: User store attribute by local claim URI, for claims that use a different attribute in this user store.

enabled.description: Whether the user store is enabled (the `Disabled` property). The default is `true`.

id.description: User store ID (base64url of the domain name).

name.description: Domain name, for example `CUSTOMERS`. Changing it replaces the user store.

properties.description: The user store's properties. A JDBC store needs `url`, `userName` and `driverName` (for example `org.postgresql.Driver`). An LDAP store needs properties such as `ConnectionURL`, `ConnectionName`, `UserSearchBase`, `UserNameAttribute` and `GroupSearchBase`. The Console and `GET /userstores/meta/types/{type-id}` list every property.

secret_properties.description: Confidential properties, such as `password` for JDBC or `ConnectionPassword` for LDAP. The server returns them encrypted, so the provider cannot notice changes made outside Terraform.

type.description: User store manager type: `UniqueIDJDBCUserStoreManager`, `UniqueIDReadOnlyLDAPUserStoreManager`, `UniqueIDReadWriteLDAPUserStoreManager` or `UniqueIDActiveDirectoryUserStoreManager`. Changing it replaces the user store.

type_id.description: Type ID used by the API.

block.description:
Manages a secondary user store. A user store can be a JDBC database, a read-only or read-write LDAP directory, or Active Directory. Users and groups in a secondary user store have the store's domain name as a prefix, for example `CUSTOMERS/alice`. In `wso2is_user`, set `user_store = "CUSTOMERS"`.

The server deploys user stores in the background, and the provider waits until the server reports the change. The provider only manages the property keys in your configuration. To import, use the user store's domain name.

regex.description: A JavaScript regular expression that the value must match (the server's `JsRegExValidator`). You cannot use it together with `rules`. Only passwords accept a regular expression. The server rejects one for `username`.

restore_on_destroy.description: Revert the field's rules to the server defaults on destroy. The default is `true`.

block.description: Sets the validation rules for usernames or passwords. In the Console, these rules are under **Login & Registration > Password Validation** and **Username Validation**. Use either rule validators or a single regular expression. When you destroy the resource, the provider sets the field's rules back to the server defaults, unless `restore_on_destroy = false`. To import, use the field name.

claims.description: The claims in the credential. Each key is a claim name in the credential. Each value is a claim of the `http://wso2.org/vc/claim` dialect, for example `{ given_name = "given_name", mail = "email" }`. To use a custom attribute, first map it into that dialect with `wso2is_external_claim`.

display_name.description: Name shown to users and wallets.

expires_in.description: Lifetime of issued credentials in seconds (at least 60).

identifier.description: Stable identifier of the credential type (published as `credential_configuration_id`), for example `EmployeeBadge`. Changing it replaces the template.

offer_id.description: ID of the credential offer the server generated for the template.

block.description: Manages a verifiable credential template (WSO2 IS 7.3 and later, OpenID for Verifiable Credential Issuance). The template describes a credential that digital wallets can request: its format, the user attributes that it carries and how long it is valid. The server creates a credential offer for the template. To import, use the template ID.

active.description: Whether events are sent. The default is `true`.

channels.description: Channel URIs to subscribe to, for example `https://schemas.identity.wso2.org/events/login`, `.../session`, `.../user`, `.../registration`, `.../token`, `.../credential`.

endpoint.description: HTTPS URL events are posted to.

event_profile.description: Event profile name. The default is `WSO2`.

event_profile_uri.description: Event profile URI. The default is `https://schemas.identity.wso2.org/events`.

secret.description: The secret that the server uses to sign each payload (`X-WSO2-Event-Signature`). The server never returns it, so the provider cannot notice changes made outside Terraform.

status.description: The webhook's status on the server: `ACTIVE`, `PARTIALLY_ACTIVE`, `INACTIVE` or `PARTIALLY_INACTIVE`. A partial status means that some channel subscriptions failed.

block.description: Manages a webhook (WSO2 IS 7.2 and later). The server sends identity events to the webhook as signed HTTP POST requests. Events include logins, sessions, changes to user accounts, registrations, tokens and credential updates. To import, use the webhook ID.

initiator_notifications.description: Notifications to the user who started the operation (events such as `onApproval`, `onRejection`).

role_ids.description: IDs of roles whose users can approve.

user_ids.description: IDs of users who can approve.

steps.description: Approval steps, in order. A step is approved by any user holding one of `role_ids` or listed in `user_ids`.

block.description:
Manages an approval workflow. A workflow is a sequence of approval steps. Users with given roles, or given users, approve each step. Attach the workflow to user and role operations with `wso2is_workflow_association`.

While a workflow is attached to an operation, such as `ADD_USER`, the operation only finishes after someone approves it. Terraform resources that perform the operation, such as `wso2is_user`, then fail, because the object does not exist yet. To import, use the workflow ID.

enabled.description: Whether the association is active. The default is `true`.

expressions.description: Expressions, all of which must match.

rules.description: Rules that decide when an operation needs approval. Approval is needed when any rule matches. A rule matches when all of its expressions match. Without rules, every operation needs approval.

block.description: Makes a user or role operation wait for approval through a `wso2is_workflow`. To import, use the association ID.

requires_authorization.description: Whether applications need authorization to request its scopes.

scope_names.description: All scope names, handy for authorizing every scope.

block.description: Looks up an API resource by ID, identifier or name. This includes the built-in management APIs, for example the APIs with the identifiers `/api/server/v1/applications` or `/scim2/Users`.

enabled.description: Whether users can sign in.

is_management_app.description: Whether it can call the management APIs.

block.description: Looks up an application by ID, name or OAuth2 client ID, for example the built-in Console or My Account application.

enabled.description: Whether it is enabled.

name.description: Name used in `authentication_sequence` (for federated ones, the identity provider name).

block.description: Lists the authenticators that login flows can use. The list includes local authenticators (use `idp = "LOCAL"` in `authentication_sequence`) and the federated authenticators of identity providers.

attribute_mappings.description: User store attribute by user store domain.

supported_by_default.description: Whether it is shown in profiles.

block.description: Reads a local claim by its claim URI.

name.description: Authenticator or connector name, for example `GoogleOIDCAuthenticator` or `SCIM2`.

block.description: Describes the properties that a federated authenticator or an outbound provisioning connector accepts. Use it when you write a `wso2is_identity_provider` configuration. Put confidential properties in `secret_properties`.

enabled.description: Whether the flow is enabled.

steps.description: JSON array of steps (empty when no flow is defined).

block.description: Reads a flow and its settings. For example, you can copy a flow that you designed in the Console into a `wso2is_flow` resource with `steps = data.wso2is_flow.signup.steps`, or save it to a file with `local_file`.
Reads a governance connector with all of its properties, their current values and their descriptions. Use it to find property names for `wso2is_governance_connector`.

name.description: Group name (without the user store prefix).

user_store.description: User store domain of `name`. The default is `PRIMARY`.

block.description: Looks up a group by ID or name.

enabled.description: Whether it is enabled.

is_primary.description: Whether it is the primary identity provider.

block.description: Looks up an identity provider (a connection in the Console) by ID or name.

enabled.description: Whether it is active.

block.description: Looks up an organization by ID or name. The search covers all organizations below the provider's organization.

audience_id.description: Organization or application ID the role belongs to (narrows a name lookup).

block.description: Looks up a role by ID or name, for example the built-in `admin` or `everyone` role. When you look up an application role by name, also set `audience_id`.

role_ids.description: IDs of the user's roles (including through groups).

user_store.description: User store domain of `username`. The default is `PRIMARY`.

block.description: Looks up a user by ID or username.
